Thanks for the loop, Olga. Quick answers and recommended copy for AP to speed vendor creation: 

1) PO vs card: Redwood accepts both. For pilots under $25k we generally allow card; for anything above that we prefer a PO or signed SOW. Since Jordan expects a PO, that aligns with our thresholds.

2) PO routing: Yes — customers can email a signed PDF PO to billing@redwood.com. Please ask them to include the HubSpot deal ID (ACME-2381) in the PO reference field; that reduces manual reconciliation. Net-30 by default for enterprise pilots unless otherwise negotiated.

3) Vendor packet contents: W-9 (attached), vendor setup form (we use the compact PDF you attached), and banking instructions. For security we provide a bank details stub in the packet and invite AP to a short validation call if they require a certified copy.

4) Marketplace: We are on AWS Marketplace (SaaS) and it does shorten vendor setup for customers who already buy through Marketplace. If Acme wants to go that route: we need their AWS account ID and confirmation that their procurement team will accept Marketplace invoices. Marketplace purchases usually route billing through AWS and remove our need to exchange bank/invoice paperwork, but there is a latency in getting the listing entitlements configured (1-3 business days).

Suggested message to AP (copy/paste):
"Attached: Redwood vendor packet (W-9 + vendor form). Please use PDF PO addressed to Redwood Inference, Inc. and email to billing@redwood.com. Include HubSpot reference ACME-2381 in the PO number field. Standard terms: Net-30. If you prefer AWS Marketplace, please reply with your AWS account ID and we will provide the offer link and entitlements instructions"

I attached a minimal banking_instructions_stub.txt and the signed W-9 to this thread.

If you'd like, Olga, I can join a 10-min call with Acme AP to validate the packet and confirm routing — reduces back-and-forth.

Thanks,
Karthik
